segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went out from there and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard him were astonished, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, and such deeds of power done through his hands?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And aren’t his sisters here with us?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they took offense at him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he could not do any deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he was amazed at their unbelief. Then he went around the surrounding villages, teaching.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He called the Twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bread, no bag, no money in their belts,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if any place does not welcome you and they will not listen to you, as you leave there shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they went out and proclaimed that people should turn back,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they drove out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: King Herod heard of it, for the name of Jesus had become well known, and people were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why the powers are at work in him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is Elijah,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and others were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “A prophet, like one of the prophets.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when Herod heard, he said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “John, the man I beheaded—he has been raised!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For it was Herod himself who had sent and had John arrested and bound in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For John had been telling Herod,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. When he listened to him he was greatly perplexed, and yet he liked to listen to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then an opportune day came, when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his nobles, his commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Herodias’s own daughter came in and danced, and she pleased Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he swore to her,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Whatever you ask me for, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She went out and said to her mother,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What should I ask for?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The head of John the Baptizer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once she hurried back in to the king and made her request:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I want you to give me, right now, the head of John the Baptist on a platter.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The king was deeply distressed, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests he did not want to refuse her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So at once the king sent an executioner with orders to bring John’s head. The man went and beheaded him in the prison,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When his disciples heard of it, they came and took away his body and laid it in a tomb.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to him everything they had done and taught.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For many were coming and going, and they did not even have a chance to eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But many saw them leaving and recognized them, and they ran there together on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he got out of the boat, he saw a large crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When it was already late, his disciples came to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This is a deserted place, and it is already late.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Send them away so that they can go to the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You give them something to eat.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are we to go and spend two hundred denarii on bread and give it to them to eat?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had found out, they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Five, and two fish.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he ordered them to have everyone recline, group by group, on the green grass.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They reclined row by row, by hundreds and by fifties.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, said the blessing, broke the loaves, and kept giving them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They all ate and were satisfied,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and of the fish as well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once he made his disciples get into the boat and go on ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the crowd away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After taking leave of them, he went off to the mountain to pray.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He saw them straining at the oars, for the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night he came toward them, walking on the sea, and he meant to pass by them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they all saw him and were terrified. But at once he spoke with them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. They were utterly astounded within themselves,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they had not understood about the loaves; rather, their hearts were hardened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored there.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they got out of the boat, people at once recognized him

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and ran about that whole region and began to carry those who were ill around on their mats to wherever they heard he was.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And wherever he went, into villages or towns or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his cloak. And all who touched it were made well.

notes.note: The Greek is the ordinary word for “power,” used here of concrete acts that display it. “Deeds of power” keeps visible the link with verse 14, where the same word describes the “powers” at work in Jesus. There is no dispute about the meaning, and “miracles,” used by many translations, is an equally acceptable rendering.

The Greek word denotes a craftsman who builds or makes things, most often in wood, though it could also cover work in stone. “Carpenter” is the traditional rendering and remains the likeliest, but some scholars prefer the broader “builder” or “craftsman.”

The traditional rendering is “repent,” which most translations keep as an established term. In modern English that word centers on feeling sorry, whereas the Greek carries the prophets’ call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. “Turn back” is used for that reason.
This is Herod Antipas, a son of Herod the Great, who ruled Galilee and Perea under Rome. His official title was tetrarch, as Matthew and Luke call him. Mark’s “king” probably reflects popular usage.

Many manuscripts read “he was saying,” which makes Herod the speaker; this is the reading behind the King James Version. The text translated here has the plural, which fits the list of popular opinions continued in verse 15. Herod’s own verdict then comes in verse 16.

The majority of later manuscripts read “he did many things,” a difference of a few letters in Greek. Several early and important manuscripts read “he was greatly perplexed,” which most modern editions and translations follow.

Some early manuscripts read “his daughter Herodias,” which would make the girl Herod’s daughter and give her the same name as her mother. The text translated here reads “the daughter of Herodias herself,” in agreement with Matthew 14:6. The Jewish historian Josephus names Herodias’s daughter by her first marriage as Salome; Mark does not name her.
The denarius was a Roman silver coin, roughly a day’s wage for a laborer (compare Matthew 20:2). The sum the disciples mention is therefore more than half a year’s pay.

The Greek repeats a word meaning “garden beds,” picturing the crowd laid out in neat plots on the grass. The matching phrase in verse 39, “group by group,” repeats a word for dinner parties. The doubled words are a Semitic way of saying “in group after group,” and the repetition is kept in English.

notes.phrase: the fourth watch of the night
notes.note: The Roman reckoning divided the night into four watches. The fourth was the last, roughly three to six in the morning, so the disciples had been rowing for most of the night.

The words can mean simply that Jesus intended to walk past the boat. Many scholars hear instead an echo of Old Testament scenes in which God “passes by” to reveal himself (Exodus 33:19–22; 1 Kings 19:11), and of Job 9:8–11, where God walks on the sea and passes by. The rendering leaves both readings open.

The Greek is literally “I am,” the ordinary way of saying “It’s me.” The same words are also God’s self-declaration in the Greek Old Testament (for example Isaiah 43:10), and in a scene of walking on the sea many interpreters think Mark intends that echo. Whether he does is disputed; the everyday sense is certain.

notes.traditional: the border of his garment; the hem of his garment
notes.note: The word can mean simply the edge of a garment. It is also the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the tassels that Jewish men wore on the corners of their cloaks in obedience to Numbers 15:38–39. Either may be meant here.

candidates.reason: Used as adjective and noun across the Gospels and translated variously as wilderness, desert, deserted, desolate, remote or lonely; the wilderness echo with Israel’s story is lost if the English varies.
Mark’s signature adverb occurs some forty times, and translators vary between immediately, at once, straightway and omission, obscuring a marked feature of his style.
The same verb means both heal and save, and the choice between “made well,” “healed” and “saved” in healing stories needs one policy across the Gospels and Acts.
Recurs through the Synoptics of Jesus and in parables, with translations ranging from “had compassion” to “felt pity” to “was moved”; readers should see it is one word.
Used of the Lake of Galilee throughout the Gospels; translations split between “sea” and “lake,” and the choice affects Old Testament echoes such as walking on the sea.

warnings: Verse 3: σκανδαλίζω is not rendered with a register form (cause to stumble; stumble / be made to stumble; fall away; take offense / give offense; be made to fall) and has no register-exception note.
